subject: May 28 QuasarPay outage — closure package and verification request
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@quasarpay.com>
Cc: ops@quasarpay.com, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: May 28 QuasarPay outage — closure package and verification request

Hi Samira —

Thank you again for your patience while our team completed the investigation into the service interruption you saw on May 28. Attached is a concise closure package: a one-page RCA summary, a minute-by-minute timeline CSV, and the action plan with owners and target dates. Key points up front: we identified a bug in the autoscaler that allowed two concurrent scale decisions to evict warmed KV cache shards under certain burst patterns, which caused elevated tail latency and a backlog of requests in your region between 01:42–02:07 PDT.

What we are delivering in this package:
- Short RCA summary (attached) describing root cause and detection telemetry.
- A reproducible test vector and mitigation checklist we used to validate the fix.
- Action items and dates for verification on both sides (Redwood + QuasarPay).

Immediate mitigations we applied (completed May 28):
- Reverted autoscaler to the safer policy to prevent dual-scale decisions.
- Rolled a hotfix that prevents KV shard eviction on scale events.
- Increased alerting sensitivity for cache-eviction anomalies.

Planned follow-ups (owners included in the attached action plan):
1) Formal post-deployment verification in your staging with our test vector — target: Jun 2 (owner: Jonas).
2) Longer-term: add a deterministic autoscaler test to our CI and a dashboard to show per-tenant cache warmth — target: Jun 18 (owner: Marissa).
3) Shared verification call and acceptance checklist — propose Jun 3 at 10:00 AM PT.

Ask: please review the attached action plan and confirm the Jun 3 verification call or propose an alternate time. Also let us know if you want the detailed timeline in a different format (we can provide a filtered view for your team).

Apologies again for the disruption — we know these incidents are costly for you and we appreciate the partnership on verification.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.com

Attachments: quasarpay_rca_summary_2026-05-28.pdf (summary), quasarpay_timeline_20260528.csv (minute-level timeline), quasarpay_action_plan_2026-05-31.md (owners/date list)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: May 28 QuasarPay outage — closure package and verification request

Thanks — I reviewed the draft attachments and made two small wording clarifications in the action plan:
- Clarified that the CI autoscaler test will run at the same load profile we used to reproduce the eviction (included test vector).
- Added a rollback verification step to the staging checklist (to confirm KV cache is preserved after scale down).

I've attached the updated action plan in-line (see file). From a timeline perspective the hotfix rollout was complete at 02:20 PDT and metrics returned to baseline by ~02:35 PDT. The key production exposure window was 01:42–02:07 PDT.

If Neha confirms the Jun 3 slot with QuasarPay, I can own the verification run and send step-by-step instructions to their ops address.

— Jonas

On Fri, 29 May 2026 at 09:12 AM Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com> wrote:
> [original message above]
From: Samira Khan <samira@quasarpay.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@quasarpay.com
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: May 28 QuasarPay outage — closure package and verification request

Thanks Neha and team — we appreciate the clear package and the quick mitigation. A couple of clarifying questions after reviewing the attachments:

1) Can you confirm whether any user-facing requests were dropped (HTTP 5xx) or whether the impact was limited to latency/backpressure? Our logs show elevated 504s for a subset of endpoints between 01:50–02:05 PDT.

2) For the Jun 3 verification run, can you include a short runbook of the steps your team will perform so our SREs can follow along? We prefer the session to be run in parallel (Redwood does the change, we monitor). 10:00 AM PT works for us pending the runbook.

If we see other anomalies while replaying our logs this morning, I will share them.

— Samira
QuasarPay, Head of Platform Ops
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@quasarpay.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, ops@quasarpay.com
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: May 28 QuasarPay outage — closure package and verification request

Samira — thanks for the quick review and the two great questions. Short answers:

1) Impact classification: at the platform layer we observed elevated tail latency and backlog; we did see a small number of user-facing 504s correlated with the busiest upstream endpoints. That is captured in the timeline CSV (column: observed_5xx_count). We will include a short summary paragraph in the RCA PDF noting the subset of endpoints and customer-visible errors.

2) Runbook: Jonas will run the verification and we will share a step-by-step runbook by EOD today in the shared Drive link (https://drive.google.com/open?id=1QSP-rca-2026). The session will be parallel — Redwood performs the staged change while QuasarPay monitors metrics and logs.

Action: please confirm the Jun 3 10:00 AM PT slot and we'll send the calendar invite and runbook.

Neha

Subject: Re: May 28 QuasarPay outage — closure package and verification request

Samira — confirmed for Jun 3 at 10:00 AM PT. Calendar invite sent to Samira + ops.

Logistics and what to expect during the verification run:
- Duration: ~45 minutes.
- Redwood will execute the staged autoscaler policy rollback in a dedicated staging cluster observed by both teams.
- Jonas will step through the test vector and then run a controlled burst to ensure cache warmth persists through scale events.
- Success criteria: no cache-eviction events, no increase in 5xxs beyond baseline, and latency P95/P99 within the pre-incident baseline.
- Post-run: we will upload the run artifacts (metrics snapshots, traces) to the Drive folder and mark the action item as complete in INF-7821.

Next steps for us (ownership):
- Jonas: own verification run and runbook (deliverable: runbook doc and pre-run checklist) — due EOD Jun 1 (complete).
- Marissa: CI test and dashboard work — owner, target Jun 18.
- Irene: coordinate a short follow-up in two weeks to review long-term mitigation progress with the QuasarPay engineering leads — target Jun 16.

Thanks again for partnering on this — we will treat the verification as the closure criterion for the customer action item.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
